title: JS/TS fixture with a real Stryker run through the tmx import path
description: User priority #3 (2026-09-26): the Stryker import path had only been tested with a hand-made report. Build a bloated TypeScript fixture (Vitest), run real Stryker with perTest coverage, import it into tmx, analyze and verify, and fix whatever the real report shape breaks. Commit a real report snapshot as a regression fixture.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A TS fixture with a bloated Vitest suite passes under npm test
A real Stryker run (coverageAnalysis perTest, json reporter) imports into tmx with per-test killedBy mapped to real test ids
analyze + verify produce a certified reduction on the real report; any importer defects found are fixed with a regression test built from the real report
Skill docs state exactly what the JS/TS path supports and what it does not

finalSummary: Added evals/fixtures/ts-bloated-cart (TypeScript, Vitest, 66 tests incl. clones, spies, private-state peeks, snapshot, timer, skip, tautology, weak asserts, and the real boundary tests). A real Stryker 10 run imports cleanly (66 tests, 77 mutants, 97.4%); analyze certifies 66 -> 10 keeping the boundary tests; verify VALID. The real runs exposed three defects, now fixed with regression tests built from the real reports (tests/data/stryker/*.json), each failing on the pre-fix engine: (1) Stryker's default bail records one killer per mutant, so most tests looked zero-signal; the importer now refuses bailed reports (disableBail: true required). (2) Stryker 10 + vitest 5 is silently vacuous (6.5% vs 97.4% on vitest 4.1); the importer detects the signature and refuses. (3) JS smell detection missed it.skip, private-state and call-count coupling, and weak asserts; now 13/13 correct on the fixture. Stryker mutants get stable keys so tmx compare is exact. languages.md documents the verified settings, the trap, the compare-based substitute for verify --rerun, and what is not supported (JS clones, auto probation).
